members.name: or3183-fix
members.prompt:
Implement the fix for Jira bug OR-3183 in the worktree `/Users/ryanducharme/dev/worktrees/OR-3183-admin-feed-kills-guidance-socket` (branch `bugfix/OR-3183-admin-feed-kills-guidance-socket`, already created and current with main). Work only in that directory. Do not use `/Users/ryanducharme/dev/orci`.

## The bug (already diagnosed and reproduced; do not re-investigate the cause)

With the `RECENTLY_ADMINISTERED_MEDS` feature flag on, `orci/src/main/webapp/src/components/RecentlyAdministeredMeds/RecentlyAdministeredMeds.tsx` (around line 190) calls `useWebsocketSubscription` on `admin/notifications/${tenantId}/${patientId}` so it can reload its list when a `orci-event/medication-administration` or `orci-event/medication-administration-cancelled` event arrives. The code has a `fixme` saying it should not use that channel.

`orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/web/websocket/SubscriptionInterceptor.java` allows that destination only for `ROLE_ADMIN` (`checkNotificationsAdminPathAccess`). For a non-admin user it throws `WebsocketSubscriptionException`; Spring answers with a STOMP ERROR frame and closes the whole connection, so the `guidance/{tenantId}/{patientId}` subscription on the same socket dies too. The client reconnects and loops. Observed frames on dev: CONNECT ok, SUBSCRIBE `admin/notifications/demo-qa/<pmrn>`, SUBSCRIBE `guidance/demo-qa/<pmrn>`, then `ERROR message:Failed to send message to ExecutorSubscribableChannel[clientInboundChannel]`, socket closed. Result: non-admin users get no pushed (scheduled/event) guidance.

The publisher side is `orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/web/websocket/NotificationsWebsocketService.java` (builds the `admin/notifications/...` destination). Guidance fan-out goes through Redis so it reaches both app instances; whatever you do must keep working when there are 2 app instances.

## What done looks like (ticket acceptance criteria)

- A non-admin user with the flag on keeps the guidance subscription and receives pushed alerts.
- The recently administered meds list still refreshes when a medication is administered or cancelled.
- The `admin/notifications/...` destination stays restricted to admins. Do NOT loosen `checkNotificationsAdminPathAccess`, and do not make refused subscriptions silently succeed.

## Design direction

The intended end state is that the home-screen component gets its "an administration happened or was cancelled" signal from a destination a tenant user is authorized for, not from the admin feed. Read the code and pick the smallest correct way to do that. Candidates to evaluate: an existing message already delivered on `guidance/{tenantId}/{patientId}`; a new tenant-scoped destination checked with the existing `checkPathAccess` tenant check; or something already in the frontend that knows an administration was saved. Keep the payload minimal: the admin notification stream carries event detail meant for the debugger timeline, and a non-admin feed should not expose more than the signal the list needs. If a new destination is added, `SubscriptionInterceptor.checkAccessOrThrow` must recognise it, with unit tests for allowed and refused cases.

Before writing new code, check for existing helpers/patterns and reuse them (how other destinations are published, how `useWebsocketSubscription` is used elsewhere, `TimelineTab.tsx` is the legitimate admin consumer and must keep working).

## Constraints

- No git write operations at all (no commit, push, branch, stash, reset). No Jira writes. I handle git and Jira.
- Project rule: do not add code comments. Leave existing comments alone unless the code they describe changes; the `fixme` goes away if the code it describes is fixed.
- No ticket numbers in code or test names.
- Do not edit any `application*.yml`. If you believe config must change, stop and say so in your report.
- Do not run anything against dev or any shared environment. Do not run the qa-suite.
- If a controller method/response changes, the OpenAPI client may need `npm run generate:api` (then prettier on generated output); avoid that route unless needed.
- Java: constructor injection, streams, `java.time`. Idiomatic Spring.

## Verification you must run and report

- Backend: unit tests for whatever you touched, at minimum the `SubscriptionInterceptor` tests and tests for any publisher you change. From the worktree root, e.g. `mvn test -pl orci -am -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` (use `-am`: a stale sibling jar in ~/.m2 otherwise hides edits to other modules). JDK: `export JAVA_HOME=$(brew --prefix openjdk)/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home`. On a CodeArtifact `401`, run `export CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN=$(aws codeartifact get-authorization-token --domain guided-clinical --domain-owner 926418967601 --query authorizationToken --output text --region us-east-2)` and retry.
- A new test that fails without your fix: confirm it by temporarily reverting the fix, watching it go red, then restoring. Say which test and what the red looked like.
- Frontend: in `orci/src/main/webapp`, `npm install` if needed, then `npm run typecheck`. Only run prettier `--write` on files you authored/changed.
- The webapp has no unit test runner; do not add one.

## Report back

Raw facts, concise: the approach chosen and why over the alternatives; every file changed; exact commands run with their real pass/fail output tails; the red-check result; anything you could not verify (in particular, the end-to-end behaviour in a browser is not something you will have verified, so say so); and any follow-ups or risks you noticed (for example other components subscribing to admin-only destinations).

members.name: or3179-report
members.prompt:
Implement Jira task OR-3179 in the worktree `/Users/ryanducharme/dev/worktrees/OR-3179-qa-report-failure-history` (branch `feature/OR-3179-qa-report-failure-history`, already created and current with main). Work only in that directory. Do not use `/Users/ryanducharme/dev/orci`.

## Background

The QA suite (Playwright, `qa-suite/`) runs after each deploy to dev via `.github/workflows/qa-suite.yml`. That workflow zips `playwright-report/`, `playwright-results.json` and `qa-steps.json` and uploads them to the app (`POST /api/admin/qa-report`). The app renders a status page at `/qa-suite-report`:

- `orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/service/QaReportService.java` — parses the bundle, keeps `Stats` (current run) and a list of `RunSummary` (history), persisted to S3. Dev runs 2 app instances; the service already refreshes from S3 by ETag (`refreshFromS3IfStale`). Keep that working.
- `orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/web/QaReportController.java` (~800 lines) — builds the HTML by string templates, with a hard-coded dark theme (hex colours inline, an SVG donut, a history section from `buildHistorySection`).
- `orci/src/main/java/com/guided/orci/web/admin/QaReportAdminController.java` — the upload endpoint.
- `qa-suite/qa-report-reporter.ts` — custom Playwright reporter that writes `qa-steps.json` (steps, screenshots, video per test).
- Tests: `QaReportServiceTest`, `QaReportControllerTest`.
- `.github/scripts/qa-suite-slack-payload.mjs` already computes failing IDs and "since last green" for Slack; look at it for reusable logic/definitions rather than inventing a second definition of "failing test ID".

Why this ticket exists: three consecutive runs failed with the same four tests (ARD-001, INS-004, MISC-001, PABX-013), all timing out in the same helper (`expectAlert` at `pages/alert.page.ts:70`, "Test timeout of 45000ms exceeded ... waiting for locator('[data-rule-id=...]')"). The report showed none of: that the set was identical across runs, which run it started on, or that the four shared one error. The decisive clue was a browser console line (`Broker reported error: Failed to send message to ExecutorSubscribableChannel[clientInboundChannel]`) and a websocket STOMP `ERROR` frame, both only reachable by unzipping a Playwright trace.

## Scope

1. **History carries detail.** Each run in history records its failing test IDs (the `PREFIX-NNN` id from the test title, e.g. `ARD-001`) and the deployed commit SHA, not just counts. At least the last 10 runs. Existing history JSON already in S3 was written without these fields and must still deserialize and render (show the run, just without the detail).
2. **New vs ongoing.** For each failing test in the current run, show whether it is new in this run or how many consecutive runs it has failed, the run/commit where it first failed in the current streak, and the last run/commit where it passed (when history reaches that far). A test failing in consecutive runs is one ongoing failure, not a new one each run.
3. **Group by shared error.** Failing tests whose error is the same are shown as one group. You need a normalisation so that errors differing only in volatile parts (the rule id inside a locator, ids, timings, ANSI colour codes) group together; the four errors above must fall into one group. Put the classification/normalisation in small pure functions that can be unit tested.
4. **Error visible on the main page** for each failing test/group, without opening the test detail page.
5. **Flaky separate from failed.** Tests that passed on retry are listed apart from failures.
6. **Failure diagnostics from the browser.** For failed tests, capture browser console errors/warnings and websocket STOMP `ERROR` frames during the test and surface them on the report (main page group and/or detail page). Work out the least invasive way to collect them in the qa-suite (a shared fixture / auto-fixture attaching to every page the test opens is likely better than touching each spec, but many specs create their own contexts via `browser.newContext`, so check what actually sees those pages). Apply the reporter's existing secret redaction to anything captured, and bound the size (dedupe repeats, cap count and length). If this turns out to need invasive changes across specs, implement the reporter/report side, stop short of mass spec edits, and say so in your report.
7. **Restyle onto the design foundation.** The clinical app's design tokens live in `orci/src/main/webapp/src/styles/_tokens.scss`, documented in `spec/design/tokens.md` (read both; also look at how the admin pages use them). The report is server-rendered Java HTML outside the Vite bundle, so decide how it gets the tokens: preferred is to reference the real token values from one place rather than copy hex codes into Java a second time, but the page must still work on dev where it is served by the Spring app (check how/whether built webapp CSS is addressable from a server-rendered page, hashed filenames included). If sharing is impractical, mirror the token values as CSS custom properties in a single block and say so. Must look right in light and dark (follow whatever mechanism the design foundation uses for mode). Replace the inline hex colours, including the donut SVG.

This is the correct moment to fix structure rather than extend it: an 800-line controller assembling HTML is doing rendering, classification and formatting in one place. Move the failure analysis (streaks, grouping, normalisation) into the service layer or a dedicated class with its own tests, and keep the controller to rendering. If you move templates to resource files, keep it simple and say why.

## Constraints

- No git write operations at all (no commit, push, branch, stash, reset). No Jira writes. I handle git and Jira.
- Project rule: do not add code comments. Leave existing comments alone unless the code they describe changes.
- No ticket numbers in code or test names.
- Do not edit any `application*.yml`. If config must change, stop and say so in your report.
- Do not run anything against dev or any shared environment, and do not upload a report anywhere.
- Everything rendered from test data (titles, errors, console text) must be HTML-escaped; the existing `escHtml` is the pattern. Console/websocket text is untrusted input.
- The report endpoint is only enabled where `tenants.demo.qa.report.enabled=true`; keep that gate.
- Java: constructor injection, streams, `Comparator` helpers, `java.time`. Records for the data model. Idiomatic Spring Boot.
- qa-suite: TypeScript; after changes run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run check:tags` in `qa-suite/`. Only run prettier `--write` on files you changed.
- Do not modify the root `README.md`. qa-suite notes go in `qa-suite/tests-readme.md` if any are needed.

## Verification you must run and report

- `QaReportServiceTest`, `QaReportControllerTest`, and new tests for the analysis code. From the worktree root, e.g. `mvn test -pl orci -am -Dtest=<Classes> -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false` (use `-am`: a stale sibling jar in ~/.m2 otherwise hides edits to other modules). JDK: `export JAVA_HOME=$(brew --prefix openjdk)/libexec/openjdk.jdk/Contents/Home`. On a CodeArtifact `401`, run `export CODEARTIFACT_AUTH_TOKEN=$(aws codeartifact get-authorization-token --domain guided-clinical --domain-owner 926418967601 --query authorizationToken --output text --region us-east-2)` and retry.
- Tests must cover: old-format history deserializing; new/ongoing/streak classification across a multi-run history including a pass in between; grouping the four example errors into one group and a genuinely different error into another; flaky kept out of failures; HTML escaping of hostile error/console text.
- Render proof: produce the main page HTML for a realistic fixture (three consecutive red runs with the same four failures after a green run, plus one flaky test) and write it to a file under the worktree's `orci/target/` so I can open it. Tell me the path. If you can screenshot it in light and dark with the Playwright already installed in `qa-suite/node_modules`, do that too and give the image paths.

## Report back

Raw facts, concise: the structure you ended with and why; every file changed/added; how tokens reach the page; how diagnostics are captured and what specs (if any) it does not cover; exact commands run with their real pass/fail output tails; paths to the rendered HTML/screenshots; anything not verified; follow-ups and risks.
